transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Jordan Klein (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Alec Zhou (Redwood CSM), Maya Lin (Argent Summit CTO), Derek O'Neal (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Gomez (Product), Kyle Hart (SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery. Customer wants fastest path to running a prototype using Redwood's hosted API, testing latency and cost at small scale, and evaluating Dedicated/VPC if compliance and P95 latency needs demand it.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call and high level goal for today, we want to understand your dev flow and what success looks like for a quick prototype using the Redwood API.
[00:22] Maya: Yep thanks, I'm Maya. our goal is to ship a conversational aid inside our product by Q2, we want to try the hosted path first. curious about free credits and how fast we can make a first call.
[00:36] Derek: Hi Derek here. we run models in-house today for batch stuff, but real-time chat is new. need to understand latency and how Redwood handles bursty traffic.
[00:48] Sofia: Sofia, PM. timeline is about 8 weeks to a prototype with measurable UX metrics. also want to know who on your side will help with the benchmark.
[01:05] Jordan: Great. Priya is our SE, she'll run the benchmark with you. quick outline: free credits for self-serve, example quickstart that gets you from signup to first successful token in under an hour, then we can run a small benchmark to measure p50/p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:28] Priya: Hey all. a couple clarifying q's: what is expected throughput for the prototype? and are there any regulatory constraints or PII concerns we should plan for?
[01:40] Maya: For the prototype, maybe 5-10 rps peak, average far lower, but P95 target under 350ms for short responses. we do have PII in some payloads, so audit logs and retention controls matter. SOC2 is a box we need checked.
[02:00] Kyle: and network-wise we prefer VPC peering for anything beyond prototype. for hosted quickstart, we can send non-sensitive samples.
[02:12] Priya: Makes sense. hosted is simplest: you sign up, we grant credits, you run the quickstart. if you need VPC we can discuss Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC options. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and predictable throughput. Private gives you control over networking and keys.
[02:35] Derek: what's the delta on latency between hosted and dedicated usually? any numbers?
[02:42] Priya: rough ballpark, hosted typically adds extra network hop and multi-tenant scheduling, so p95 might be 1.1-1.4x of well-tuned dedicated, for chat-style models with small contexts. but in practice we often get below 400ms p95 on hosted for short prompts. dedicated with optimized quantization and kernel selection can drop that further. also caching/prefix KV helps in interactive use-cases.
[03:05] Maya: okay that's helpful. and cost? cost-benefit guidance when to flip from hosted to dedicated?
[03:12] Jordan: Cost breakpoints depend on QPS and token volumes. we can model estimated token spend vs reserved instance commit. typical threshold we see is when sustained peak usage grows beyond a few hundred rps or predictable latency is required, Dedicated starts to look compelling. we'll send a back-of-envelope pricing comparison.
[03:30] Sofia: About the quickstart: how are the credits redeemed, and is there an expiration?
[03:36] Jordan: Credits are applied to your self-serve account, usually valid for 90 days. they cover hosted usage; for Dedicated/Private pilots we have different trial arrangements and can tie to an enterprise POC quote.
[03:50] Derek: For benchmarks, can SE test with our payloads? we have a couple of real convo traces.
[03:56] Priya: Yes, please share sanitized traces. we'll run 95th-percentile latency and token-cost analysis. also want to know sequence lengths, typical system prompt size, and whether you plan to stream responses.
[04:12] Derek: We'll sanitize and share a 500 request sample.
[04:16] Kyle: quick question on security: do you support SSO/SAML for admin access and can we integrate our KMS for key rotation?
[04:25] Alec: On the CSM side, we handle SSO/SAML for console access and RBAC. For key management, Hosted uses our managed keying but we offer Dedicated/Private with KMS integrations for enterprise. audit logs are available and retention can be configured for Dedicated/Private customers.
[04:44] Maya: Is Redwood SOC2 certified today?
[04:48] Jordan: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II. we'll share the compliance pack after this call.
[04:55] Sofia: Great. any gotchas with streaming vs non-streaming on token accounting?
[05:01] Priya: You are billed per token generated and per token input; streaming doesn't change token accounting but can increase perceived latency by returning tokens earlier. batching and caching can lower cost but might add latency; it's a trade.
[05:20] Derek: For the prototype we probably won't use aggressive quantization, but for Dedicated we might explore q4/q5 quantization to cut GPU cost.
[05:30] Priya: Exactly, we can recommend quantization and kernel profiles based on your model and sequence lengths.
[06:00] Jordan: Let's walk through a suggested onboarding: 1) Sign up self-serve account, 2) apply credits we give you, 3) run quickstart with sample repo, 4) schedule benchmark with SE, 5) follow decision tree for Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private depending on latency/compliance.
[06:20] Maya: That workflow looks good. can you demo the quickstart steps briefly?
[06:27] Jordan: Sure I can share the quickstart link in chat, it's basically an SDK call and a curl example. most customers get a first successful generation inside 20-30 minutes if they have environment access.
[06:45] Priya: I'll also attach a small benchmark harness that you can run locally before our SE session.
[06:53] Sofia: What about rate limits and burst handling on hosted?
[06:58] Priya: Hosted has per-account rate limits but we allow temporary bursts and can increase limits for pilots. if you expect sustained bursts of many rps, Dedicated offers dedicated GPUs to keep latency predictable.
[07:20] Derek: one more on observability — does Redwood expose token-level traces and per-route latency in the console?
[07:28] Alec: Yes, the console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and exportable traces for your own observability stack.
[07:40] Maya: About data retention: if we use hosted for prototype, where does the data live and can we disable retention?
[07:48] Jordan: For hosted, short-term logs are retained for debugging and then purged; Dedicated/Private gives finer control over retention and the ability to disable persisting payloads. we'll share the data retention policy doc.
[08:05] Kyle: Regarding VPC peering for Private — is that supported in specific cloud regions? we run in us-west-2 primarily.
[08:12] Priya: Yes, VPC peering and private deployments are available in major cloud regions including us-west-2; depending on your network setup we'll coordinate with infra to provision peering.
[08:26] Derek: Any minimums for Dedicated? commits?
[08:29] Jordan: Dedicated has reserve commits and we can tailor a pilot (short-term reserved) to avoid annual lock-in for initial evaluation. we'll outline options in the pricing doc.
[08:45] Sofia: Competitor question — how does Redwood compare to doing everything in-house on our GPUs?
[08:50] Priya: In-house gives control but you take on operational burden: kernel optimization, quantization engineering, scaling, batching, and maintaining low latency under load. Redwood provides the runtime optimizations, kernel selection, and routing, plus the console for observability, which usually shortens time-to-production. Price break-even depends on utilization and ops headcount.
[09:18] Maya: Can you give an example of a customer that started hosted and moved to Dedicated? any timeline?
[09:24] Jordan: We had a fintech customer that prototyped on hosted for about 6 weeks, then after validating UX moved to Dedicated to meet stricter p95 and throughput needs. we can share an anonymized case study.
[09:40] Derek: going back to demo steps, can Priya walk through a minimal curl example?
[09:44] Priya: Sure — (gives a short curl with api-key header, model, prompt). It's basically: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' -d '{"model":"rwd-small-1","input":"Hello"}'
[10:05] Sofia: Great. any pitfalls when integrating from a frontend? like CORS or streaming websocket support?
[10:12] Priya: We recommend proxying calls through your backend for keys and rate limits. streaming via SSE or websocket is supported but again keys should stay server-side.
[10:28] Maya: For the benchmark, our important metric is P95 under production-like payloads. Derek will prepare payloads and configs.
[10:36] Derek: yes will do.
[10:40] Priya: We'll need sequence length distribution, example system prompts, expected concurrency, and whether generation is streamed.
[10:49] Kyle: can Redwood help with a short perf test script we can run in our staging before the SE session?
[10:55] Priya: Yes we'll share a lightweight harness and also run a managed benchmark when you're ready.
[11:12] Jordan: I want to cover success criteria for the pilot — what do you need to see to move from prototype to pilot?
[11:20] Sofia: For us: 1) p95 < 350ms for typical user flows, 2) cost estimates within budget for Q3 scale, 3) compliance docs and SSO set, and 4) a plan for eventual VPC if needed.
[11:36] Maya: Also visibility into token-level cost by route so Product can evaluate unit economics.
[11:44] Alec: Absolutely — console + cost breakdown will be part of the pilot.
[11:50] Derek: If during benchmark we see higher latency, what's the typical remediation path?
[11:55] Priya: We first check model variant and sequence lengths, enable caching or reduce prompt size, then look at Dedicated buildouts: optimized kernels, quantization, and reserved GPU capacity. We can also recommend model variants that are faster for short contexts.
[12:20] Maya: On compliance — will you share SOC2 docs and data processing addendum?
[12:25] Jordan: Yes we'll upload the compliance pack; I'll send the link after the call.
[12:30] Sofia: Ok that's helpful. can we get an estimate for how long a hosted quickstart takes for full-stack dev to demo? like dev to first integrated call?
[12:38] Jordan: Typical is 20-60 minutes — most teams hit first generate within 30 minutes if they follow the quickstart and have network access.
[12:48] Derek: for streaming UX we might need a sample server-side implementation — do you have snippets?
[12:53] Priya: Yes we have sample code for SSE and websockets in the quickstart repo.
[13:05] Maya: Any special notes on rate limiting in early trials? we don't want throttling to affect the demo.
[13:10] Jordan: During demo/pilot we can raise soft limits to ensure you can demo. for production we'll set limits appropriate to your plan.
[13:25] Sofia: What about model rollouts/versions — how do you handle pinned versions?
[13:31] Priya: You can pin model versions per route and rollout via canaries/A-B. Redwood supports automatic fallback to compatible variants in case of model failures.
[13:45] Derek: Great. let's talk data residency — can we keep logs within our region?
[13:50] Alec: In Dedicated/Private yes; hosted is in our region clusters — we'll confirm exact region placement for your account.
[14:05] Kyle: Network egress concerns: for Private we want minimal external egress, any limits?
[14:12] Priya: Private can be built air-gapped or with restricted egress; we'll need to scope with infra.
[14:30] Jordan: quick check — are there any blockers to starting the self-serve trial this week?
[14:35] Maya: none on our side, we'll need the credits and the quickstart link. Derek and I will coordinate on payload sanitization.
[14:44] Jordan: Great. I'll send credits and the quickstart repo after the call. Priya will schedule the benchmark session.
[14:52] Sofia: timeline wise, if we start trial this week, when can we expect the SE benchmark?
[14:58] Priya: We can do the benchmark within 1-2 business weeks after we receive payloads and account access.
[15:10] Derek: fine.
[15:15] Maya: Any final questions on architecture?
[15:18] Kyle: one minor: does Redwood support custom plugins or tool-calls? we may want to connect to internal vector DB later.
[15:25] Priya: We support function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs; integrations with vector DBs are straightforward — many customers pair Redwood with their embeddings store.
[15:40] Sofia: Ok sounds good.
[15:44] Jordan: we'll wrap up with explicit next steps. Jordan to send pricing, credits, compliance pack. Priya to kick off SE benchmark scheduling and send the sample harness. Maya to share sanitized traces and traffic targets.
[16:02] Maya: We'll get those to you by Friday.
[16:06] Jordan: Thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.

(rough end of transcript)
notes: Customer favors hosted quickstart to validate UX quickly, but serious about Dedicated/Private if latency or compliance demands scale.
SE will run benchmark with sanitized payloads; pricing doc to include cost breakpoints for Dedicated vs Hosted.
